jurisdiction.overview: Nationally published records appear separately from applicable EU-level records. The landscape, historical relationships and legal applicability remain under document-level review.

narrative.summary: Singapore governs AI mainly through guidance and testing rather than an AI-specific law, under its National AI Strategy 2.0 (2023, updated 2026). IMDA and the PDPC publish the Model AI Governance Framework (2020) and its versions for generative AI (2024) and agentic AI (2026), the AI Verify testing framework, a starter kit for testing LLM applications, generative AI evaluation and assurance sandboxes, and 2026 transparency guidelines for generative AI chatbots. Binding rules touching AI include the Personal Data Protection Act, with PDPC advisory guidelines on personal data in AI systems (2024) and generative AI (2026), a ban on deepfakes of election candidates (in force January 2025), 2025 criminal offences on AI-generated intimate images and computer-generated child abuse material, the Online Safety (Relief and Accountability) Act 2025, the copyright exception for computational data analysis, and autonomous-vehicle trial rules. Regulators are active: MAS issued Guidelines on AI Risk Management in October 2026 (effective October 2027) on top of its FEAT principles and Veritas methodology, CSA publishes guidelines on securing AI systems and agentic AI, HSA regulates machine-learning medical devices and runs an AI medical app exemption, and MOH, the Ministry of Law and the courts have sector AI guidance. Singapore Standards adopt ISO/IEC 42001 and add technical references on AI security and LLM cybersecurity.
lead_institutions: Ministry of Digital Development and Information
narrative.review_notes: Deep review completed on 11 October 2026 at national level, covering laws, the digital ministry and IMDA, the Smart Nation Group and GovTech, ministries and the courts, regulators, and national standards and sandboxes. Singapore Standards are recorded from their official catalogue entries, as their full texts are sold. Some documents were not published or not dated, including the Government's public-sector AI playbooks, internal circulars on government use of large language models and the first edition of the Model AI Governance Framework; these are held as pending. Pending: the commencement of the online impersonation and inauthentic-material provisions of the Online Safety Act, the 2026 bill on autonomous vehicles, IPOS guidance on examining AI patent applications, and the updated cybersecurity codes of practice.

instruments.official_title: Guidelines and Companion Guide on Securing AI Systems
instruments.english_title: Guidelines and Companion Guide on Securing AI Systems
instruments.current_status: Published 15 October 2024 (CSA page date; both PDFs dated October 2024). Companion Guide version history: v0.1 draft released for consultation 29 July 2024, v1.0 first release 15 October 2024. CSA states both are 'living resources' to be updated. Extended by the Securing Agentic AI addendum (v1.0, 17 June 2026). The Guidelines state they are not mandatory.
instruments.summary: CSA guidelines for system owners on securing AI systems across a five-stage lifecycle (planning and design, development, deployment, operations and maintenance, end of life), starting with a risk assessment, against both classical cyber risks (e.g. supply-chain attacks) and adversarial machine learning (data poisoning, evasion, inference and extraction attacks). The companion guide is a community-driven, non-prescriptive compilation of practical controls per lifecycle stage mapped to MITRE ATLAS and OWASP references. The Guidelines expressly exclude AI safety, fairness, transparency and the misuse of AI (e.g. deepfakes) and are not mandatory.

instruments.english_title: Advisory Guidelines on use of Personal Data in AI Recommendation and Decision Systems
instruments.current_status: Issued 1 March 2024 (date on the cover and on the PDPC page). Advisory guidelines issued by the Commission; they state that they are advisory, not legally binding on the Commission or any other party, and that the PDPA prevails over them. Proposed version issued for public consultation on 18 July 2023 (comments closed 31 August 2023); PDPC response to feedback issued 1 March 2024. Supplemented (not replaced) by the Advisory Guidelines on Use of Personal Data in Generative AI issued 20 July 2026.
instruments.summary: Clarifies how the Personal Data Protection Act 2012 applies when organisations use personal data to develop, test, monitor and deploy systems that embed machine-learning models to make recommendations, predictions or decisions. It sets criteria for relying on the Business Improvement and Research exceptions instead of consent during development, explains consent, notification and accountability obligations at deployment (including what to tell consumers and written policies on safeguards), and recommends best practices for third-party service providers acting as data intermediaries, such as data mapping, labelling and provenance records.

instruments.english_title: Model AI Governance Framework for Agentic AI
instruments.current_status: First published (v1.0) on 22 January 2026, announced by the Minister for Digital Development and Information at the World Economic Forum (MDDI press release). Current version 1.5, 'Published 20 May 2026 (Updated 5 June 2026)', incorporates feedback from 60+ companies and adds case studies (including IMDA's OpenClaw case study), systemic and multi-agent risks and automation-bias practices. Voluntary guidance; IMDA describes it as a living document.
instruments.scope: Organisations in Singapore and elsewhere that deploy agentic AI, whether developed in-house or from third parties
instruments.summary: IMDA's voluntary framework for deploying AI agents responsibly, built on the 2020 Model AI Governance Framework. It sets out measures across four dimensions: assessing and bounding risks upfront (use-case selection, limits on agents' autonomy, tools and permissions), making humans meaningfully accountable (allocating responsibilities along the agentic value chain and defining checkpoints requiring human approval), implementing technical controls and testing across the agent lifecycle, and enabling end-user responsibility through transparency and training. Version 1.5 (May/June 2026) adds case studies, systemic and multi-agent risks, and practices to guard against automation bias.

instruments.english_title: Online Safety (Relief and Accountability) Act 2025
instruments.current_status: Act 23 of 2025, passed 5 November 2025, assented 25 November 2025 and first published in the Gazette 8 December 2025; partly in force from 29 June 2026 under S 394/2026 and S 395/2026, with implementing regulations S 396-403/2026 and S 411-413/2026 made in June 2026. Section 15 (online impersonation), section 16 (inauthentic material abuse) and the related torts (ss 85-86) had not been brought into operation as at 11 October 2026.
instruments.summary: Establishes a Commissioner of Online Safety (the Online Safety Commission) who can receive reports and direct communicators, administrators and online service providers to stop or remedy specified online harms, and creates statutory torts so victims can sue. Its harm definitions expressly reach AI-generated content: "intimate image abuse" covers images or recordings "altered or generated by any means", with generative-AI creation of a realistic sexual depiction given as an illustration (in force 29 June 2026), and "inauthentic material abuse" covers realistic, digitally altered or generated false depictions of a person, naming generative AI as an example and treating prominent AI-generated labels as relevant (not yet in operation).
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Online-harms statute that directly covers deepfake intimate images and other AI-generated inauthentic material.
instruments.evidence_reference: sgp-deep-review-S1-2026-10-11. instruments.english_title: Criminal Law (Miscellaneous Amendments) Act 2025
instruments.current_status: Act 21 of 2025, passed 4 November 2025, assented 25 November 2025 and first published in the Gazette 3 December 2025; it commences in tranches: first tranche 30 December 2025, the Penal Code amendments on intimate images and child abuse material (ss 49-53 of the Act) on 17 August 2026 according to the Ministry of Home Affairs (press release of 14 August 2026), and the remaining provisions later. The Act text does not use the term "artificial intelligence"; MHA describes the amendments as covering AI-generated material.
instruments.summary: Omnibus criminal-law amendment Act. For AI it amends the Penal Code so that an "intimate image or recording" includes one that has been "generated" (not only altered), creates a new offence of intentionally producing an intimate image of a person without consent (up to 2 years' imprisonment, fine or both; mandatory imprisonment and possible caning where the person is under 14), and clarifies that "child abuse material" covers material whether or not any child was involved in its production, including realistic images of fictional persons.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Criminalises non-consensual production of AI-generated intimate images (deepfakes) and computer-generated child abuse material.

instruments.english_title: Road Traffic (Amendment) Act 2017
instruments.current_status: Act 10 of 2017, passed 7 February 2017, assented 13 March 2017, first published 21 March 2017; commenced in stages. The autonomous-vehicle provisions now in ss 6C-6E of the Road Traffic Act 1961 are in operation from 24 August 2017 (SSO provision timeline). Section 6C(3), as amended by Act 12 of 2021 (from 30 September 2021), provides that s 6C and all rules under it continue in force only until the end of 24 August 2027.
instruments.summary: Amends the Road Traffic Act to define autonomous motor vehicles and autonomous systems (operation without active physical control or monitoring by a human) and to let the Minister make rules for the Land Transport Authority to authorise trials of automated vehicle technology and special uses of autonomous vehicles on public roads despite normal driver requirements. The rules may require liability insurance or security, public notice of trials, sensor-data and video recording, failure alerts allowing immediate manual takeover, record-keeping and data sharing, with suspension or cancellation of authorisations; the regime is time-limited (now to 24 August 2027).
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Primary legislation enabling a regulatory sandbox for autonomous (AI-driven) vehicles on Singapore roads.

instruments.official_title: Copyright Act 2021
instruments.english_title: Copyright Act 2021
instruments.current_status: Act 22 of 2021, first published in the Gazette 7 October 2021 (SSO Acts Supplement listing). Sections 243-244 in operation from 21 November 2021 (SSO provision timeline); 2020 Revised Edition from 31 December 2021. Current SSO version as at 9 March 2025.
instruments.summary: Singapore's copyright statute. Division 8 of its permitted uses (ss 243-244) creates a computational data analysis exception: a person with lawful access to a work or recording may copy it, without the owner's permission, to identify, extract and analyse data or to use it as examples to improve a computer program (the Act's illustration is training a program to recognise images), provided the copy is used only for that purpose and shared only to verify results or for collaborative research. Lawful access excludes circumventing paywalls or breaching database terms of use, and the exception cannot be overridden by contract (s 187).
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Statutory text-and-data-mining exception that permits copying for AI/machine-learning training.

instruments.summary: IMDA practical reference for organisations testing agentic AI systems for safety and reliability, under the technical-controls dimension of the Model AI Governance Framework for Agentic AI. It sets out a four-step approach: identify relevant risks such as erroneous or unauthorised actions, build realistic tests with harnesses, logging and agent-specific metrics, run tests and analyse logs, and monitor and re-test continuously. It includes case studies from deployers and testers.

coverage_audit.no_material_found_note: Singapore's laws, the government and ministries, regulators, standards and sandboxes were searched. No AI procurement guidance or clauses have been published (undated government technology playbooks are listed as leads), and no government-published AI readiness index was found. Some national standards are recorded from catalogue entries and free previews only, because their full texts are paid.
coverage_audit.technical_note:
Coverage note (original): Technical review notes: Backfill run 2026-10-11 at national level only (PROTOCOL §6) in four parts (S1 laws; S2 government incl. ministry-level search; S3 regulators; S4 standards and sandboxes). No usage-limit interruption; the four earlier records were re-checked and fixed (the agentic AI record now points to the framework, not the press release; site-name prefixes and domain-named publishers removed). curl worked on almost every site; Singapore Statutes Online throttled repeated requests (paused requests succeeded) and enterprisesg.gov.sg needed WebFetch. Located-only (11): Singapore Standards and Technical References read from eShop catalogue entries and free previews (full texts paid; year-only dates). Overlaps resolved: PDPC synthetic data guide and SGH/Kajima practical guidance (S1/S3), AV Rules 2017 (S1/S4), Starter Kit (S2/S4), AIHGle 2.0 (S2/S3) recorded once; duplicate events dropped. Third-party host: IMDA pages name aiverifyfoundation.sg as where the GenAI framework and the 2023 discussion paper are published (PROTOCOL §1). The Singapore Consensus on Global AI Safety Research Priorities is recorded from the Government's SCAI site. The Criminal Law (Miscellaneous Amendments) Act 2025 commencement (17 Aug 2026) is from the Ministry of Home Affairs release; the SSO commencement notification was not read. procurement: no AI procurement guidance or clauses published (GovTech playbooks undated, leads). index-readiness: no government-published AI readiness index.

Catch-up sweep 2026-10-19: checked IMDA press releases, CSA advisories and press releases (to 15 Oct 2026), PDPC announcements, MAS (search), MDDI (search). Found i-313a2837685b (IMDA Starter Kit for Testing Agentic Systems, 14 Oct 2026); leads: AI Verify Foundation AI Tester Accreditation Programme and CSA SICW 2026 agentic AI tabletop outcome statement. Ruled out: CSA quantum-safe advisory, cyber workforce study and accreditation framework, MoUs (not AI instruments); IMDA FAIRS taskforce (sector taskforce, no document). IPOS AI and IP consultation (i-57bbf1283c6e) still open until 22 Oct 2026. Not reached: none.
